concepts.why: Textual / Lutheran / Reformed / Catholic / Orthodox: neither passage says 'new'; both say the old heavens and earth wear out, vanish or are 'changed' (Ps 102:26 'Like clothing You will change them'). Set under 'New heavens and a new earth' they imply the old is replaced, which is the very point on which Lutherans (the present earth passes away) part from Reformed, Catholic and Orthodox readers (the present earth is renewed). Move both to a secondary line such as 'The heavens and the earth -> wear out like a garment' (Ps 102:25-26; Isa 51:6), where they state what they state and nothing about what follows. The four remaining passages all say 'new heavens/heaven and a new earth' or 'first heaven and earth had passed away'. All notes are exact quotations.

Name against passages: the name is 'groaning', but Isa 24:4 and Jer 12:4 say the earth/land 'mourns' (Jer 12:4 gives the cause as 'the evil of its residents', Isa 24 is a judgment passage), and Rom 8:23 says 'we ourselves' groan, not the creation. Keep Rom 8:19-22 as the concept; move Isa 24:4 and Jer 12:4 to a secondary line 'The earth -> mourns and withers' (the OT beside the NT with no claim that one explains the other); Rom 8:23 stays under concept 7 where it is already listed (and could also be offered here only if the name were 'groaning' of creation and of us). Notes in 8:19, 8:20-21, 8:22 are exact.

concepts.name: A new heart
concepts.why: Name against passages: 'I will give you a new heart' is Ezek 36:26 only; Ezek 18:31 is a command to Israel to make themselves a new heart, Ps 51:10 is David's prayer ('clean heart'), Jer 31:33 and 24:7 do not say 'new' at all but 'law inscribed on their hearts' and 'a heart to know Me'. A plain label in the texts' word, 'A new heart', holds all six (Ezek 11:19, 18:31, 36:26 say 'new spirit'/'heart of flesh'; Jer and Ps are the heart renewed) without the name asserting that God gives it in every one (Wesleyan/Baptist reader: 18:31 puts the doing on the hearer; Reformed reader: 36:26 on God; the label takes neither side). Keep 'I will give you a new heart' as the note on Ezek 36:26. All six notes are exact quotations.

Passage holds the concept: 2 Cor 4:16 says the inner self 'is being renewed day by day'; it says nothing of creating or of a new creation, it is the renewal line already carried by the secondary 'The mind -> renewed'. Move it there. (Eph 2:10 says 'created' but not 'new'; it is acceptable because the verse speaks of being created in Christ Jesus, as 2 Cor 5:17 speaks of being in Christ.) Notes are exact. Note too that Eph 4:24 and Col 3:10 are also carried in the secondary 'The old self -> the new self'; the duplication is harmless but could be trimmed from whichever line is shorter.

Passage holds the concept: 1 John 3:2 says 'we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is' when Christ appears; it does not speak of bodies, rising, or the imperishable, so it shares a theme (becoming like Christ) rather than the concept. Put it with concept 10's 'They will see His face' neighbourhood or in a secondary line 'Like Him -> we will see Him as He is' (with Phil 3:21 if wished). Isa 26:19 is acceptable here: the BSB reads 'Your dead will live; their bodies will rise' (secular/Jewish readers dispute whether the verse speaks of individual resurrection, but the text says it in these words and no claim of fulfilment is made). Notes exact.

Secular academic / Jewish reader of the Hebrew Bible: in its own context Hosea 13:14 is widely read as God summoning death's plagues against Ephraim (the BSB verse itself ends 'Compassion is hidden from My eyes'), not as the destruction of death. It speaks of death being defeated only when read through 1 Cor 15:55, which is exactly a New Testament reading laid over an OT verse. Drop it from this concept, and either leave it out or put it in a secondary line citing 1 Cor 15:54-55 together with it, without saying one fulfils the other. Isa 25:8, 1 Cor 15:26, 15:54-55, Rev 20:14, 21:4 all hold the concept; notes exact. Rev 20:14 takes no side on the order of the last things as it only says Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire.

Name against passages and as nine readers would take it: the name ('New Jerusalem, prepared as a bride') is said only by Rev 3:12 and 21:2. Isa 65:18 says 'I will create Jerusalem' (no 'new', and Baptist/dispensational readers take it as the earthly Jerusalem of the age to come, Reformed and Catholic readers as the same city as Rev 21); Gal 4:26 'the Jerusalem above', Heb 12:22 'the heavenly Jerusalem' and Heb 11:10 / 13:14 'the city with foundations / the city that is to come' are different phrases. Putting them all under the Revelation phrase says each of them is the new Jerusalem, which is the side. Keep Rev 3:12 and 21:2 (add Rev 21:10 'the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven'). Move Gal 4:26, Heb 11:10, 12:22, 13:14 to a new concept in their own words (see missing: 'The city that is to come'); Isa 65:18 goes to concept 1's neighbour or stays on the front page's table. Notes exact.

Passage holds the concept: the name is God's dwelling with man (Lev 26:11, Ezek 37:27, Zech 2:10, Rev 21:3); John 14:2-3 has Jesus going to prepare a place so that disciples may be where he is, the other direction (people to the Father's house), and it is a verse readers divide on (heaven at death, the Lord's return, the Spirit's indwelling in 14:23). Its note 'In My Father's house are many rooms' also does not say what the concept says. Drop it. Lev 26:11-12, Ezek 37:27, Zech 2:10, 2 Cor 6:16, Rev 21:3, 21:22, 22:4 all fit; notes exact. 2 Cor 6:16 (the church as temple of the living God now) beside Rev 21 is fine because it quotes Lev 26:12 and the note says only what the verse says.

Passage holds the concept: Ezek 47:12 does not say 'tree of life' (fruit trees of all kinds, leaves for healing). Setting it under a name it does not contain asserts the link from Ezekiel to Revelation 22:2 as the text's own; keep it in the secondary 'The river' line where it belongs, with Rev 22:2. Add the passages that do say 'tree of life': Proverbs 3:18 ('She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her'), 11:30, 13:12, 15:4 (see missing: none needed beyond the tree itself). Notes in Gen 2:9, 3:24, Rev 2:7, 22:2, 22:14 are exact.

secondary_or_links: The former things -> not remembered, passed away: Isaiah 43:19 does not contain the phrase; its predecessor Isa 43:18 does ('Do not call to mind the former things'). Cite Isaiah 43:18-19 so the line's own words appear in the passage.

God -> all in all: 1 Corinthians 15:24-28 is a five-verse run; the concept is in v28 ('so that God may be all in all'); cut to 15:28, with 15:27-28 at most. The longer run opens the Son handing over the kingdom, a matter on which readers of the order of the last things differ.

All things -> renewed, restored: Matthew 19:28 ('the renewal of all things') and Acts 3:21 ('the restoration of all things') are two different words in the original; the line is acceptable because it only lists both English words, but state them as two phrases on the card, not one idea.

Add a secondary line 'The heavens and the earth -> wear out like a garment' carrying Psalm 102:25-26 and Isaiah 51:6 (moved from concept 1), and a line 'The earth -> mourns and withers' carrying Isaiah 24:4 and Jeremiah 12:4 (moved from concept 2). Add Ezekiel 47:12 to the line 'The river -> the water of life'.

Links: restore 'Judgment' (Daniel 12:2, John 5:28-29, Revelation 20:14 all speak of judgment alongside the new) -- the drafter's cut was made only because the concepts that used it were removed, but the secondary line 'The dead -> to life or to judgment' still depends on it. 'Resurrection' (if the site has such a theme) should also be linked, since concept 7 rests on it. The other ten links are supported by their passages.

missing.sub_theme: The city that is to come
missing.why: The passages dropped from concept 9 are a plain sub-theme in their own words: a city looked for, the Jerusalem above. Stated as phrases from the texts, with no statement that it is the New Jerusalem of Revelation 21.

missing.sub_theme: Born again / born of the Spirit
missing.why: The texts' own phrase for the beginning of new life, plainly belonging to this theme and a section on which readers (Baptist, Lutheran, Wesleyan, Catholic, Pentecostal) vary only about the means, which a heading using the texts' words does not decide. Titus 3:5 is currently inside 'The Spirit gives life' and could be shared.

missing.sub_theme: There will be no more night
missing.why: The renewed city's light ('the Lamb is its lamp', 'no more night') is developed alongside 'the sea was no more' and 'no longer any curse' and is a standard strand of what is made new; Isaiah 60:19-20 gives the OT words.

The word 'new' with covenant is plainly developed in the texts; the site may prefer to keep it under the Covenant theme (it is linked), in which case say so on the Covenant page and leave only the link here. Offered as a candidate with lower weight than the first three.
